text:
The Blackhawks won 6-3, and the only thing anyone in Chicago will ask about this morning is Connor Bedard. Daily Faceoff reported that Bedard left with an upper-body injury after 12 minutes of ice time, and The Athletic's Mark Lazerus framed the night as a chaotic win shadowed by "another Connor Bedard absence." He had just scored the goal that put Chicago ahead for good. For the Maple Leafs, the night simply extended the worst stretch of Jim Hiller's first season behind their bench: seven straight losses.

This one was closer than the score. Expected goals (the quality of each team's chances) finished 3.21 to 3.15, and our replays of every shot give Chicago the win only 51% of the time. Toronto led early on Easton Cowan's snap shot, set up by Auston Matthews, and carried more of the play through two periods. Matthews put six shots on goal and the Leafs out-chanced Chicago 2.01 to 0.85 with him on the ice. It did not matter.

Frank Nazar tied it on the power play and then gave Chicago the lead at 17:54 of the second. Teddy Blueger answered 22 seconds later on a shot with under a 1% chance of going in, and 35 seconds after that Bedard's wrister lifted the Hawks' win chance from 52% to 75%. In the third, Tyler Bertuzzi tipped in a power-play goal, John Tavares scored off a feed from rookie Gavin McKenna in his first NHL meeting with Bedard, and Oliver Moore restored the two-goal cushion 12 seconds later. Bertuzzi finished it at 12:10. Sam Rinzel had three assists from the blue line.

The difference was in net. Spencer Knight stopped 31 of 34, about what those shots deserved. Sergei Bobrovsky allowed six on 25, 2.8 goals more than expected, and Chicago went 2 for 3 on the power play while Toronto went 0 for 3. When a losing streak gets this long, nights like this feel cruel: the Leafs did enough to win half of these games and got nothing.

Chicago is now 2-0-1 since The Summit, as Lazerus noted. Whether that run survives depends on the update the Blackhawks give on Bedard.
headline: Hawks pile on the Leafs, then hold their breath on Bedard
